lessons.text: The working directory's project changes between sessions: it may be a small pure-Python package such as `inventory/` or `shapes/` (with tests in `tests/`, run by `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v`). Always read the tree first and match the conventions of sibling modules; do not trust a remembered package name, and do not assume a `CHANGELOG.md` exists.
lessons.evidence: Lesson #0 asserted the project was the `inventory` package, but this session's tree was `shapes/square.py` + empty `shapes/__init__.py` with no `tests/`; I had to `ls` and read `shapes/square.py` to learn the style, so the concrete package name in the lesson was misleading.

lessons.text: This project's CI (`regression-tests` check) fails a bug-fix PR that has no test whose name starts with `test_regression_`; name the test for the fixed bug that way.
lessons.evidence: CI report rejected my Stock.remove fix with "bug-fix PR contains no test named `test_regression_*`" even though all functional tests passed; adding `test_regression_remove_more_than_available` addresses it.

lessons.text: This repo's CI runs a `license-header` check requiring `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` as the first line of each new Python file (above imports); it did not flag the pre-existing `shapes/square.py`, so only added files need it. There is no CI config in the tree — reports arrive as text, so run the checks you can't see from `.github/`.
lessons.evidence: CI report: "✗ license-header: shapes/circle.py:1: missing `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`" after I wrote shapes/circle.py with `import math` on line 1; adding the header fixed it, while header-less shapes/square.py was never flagged.

lessons.text: This repo's CI lint rule L001 forbids `print` and `warnings.warn` in library code: warning about a runtime condition must go through a module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (e.g. `logger.warning(...)`), and tests must capture it with `assertLogs`/`assertNoLogs`.
lessons.evidence: CI report on the missing-config change: "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)". Reworked loader/config.py to a module logger and tests/test_config.py to assertLogs; tests pass.

lessons.text: When creating the first `tests/` file in this repo, also add `tests/__init__.py` (with the `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` header); otherwise `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` fails with `ImportError: Start directory is not importable`.
lessons.evidence: In this session `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` first failed with `ImportError: Start directory is not importable: '.../tests'` because the repo had no `tests/` package; adding `tests/__init__.py` (header included per lesson #2) made discovery run the 2 tests.

lessons.text: End every final report of a turn with a line `Risk: low|medium|high`, on its own line, as the very last line (e.g. `Risk: low`), because the `release-bot` CI check fails the change when the final report has no such line.
lessons.evidence: CI report after the greet() change: "✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end", while the tests check passed.

lessons.text: Before ending a turn with a change, self-check the known CI gates of this repo, since no CI config exists in the tree: (1) every added .py file starts with `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`; (2) no `print`/`warnings.warn` in library code (L001: use a module logger); (3) a bug-fix PR includes a test named `test_regression_*`; (4) if you created tests/, it has `tests/__init__.py`; (5) every new or changed function has full type annotations and a docstring (mypy/pydocstyle gate, even if sibling functions lack them); (6) error paths raise the package's own error class from its `errors.py`, not a builtin (the `error-policy` check); (7) the final report ends with a `Risk: low|medium|high` line.
lessons.evidence: This session's CI report listed a gate the checklist lacked: "✓ error-policy", which passed only because validate_age raises the package's AppError from users/errors.py rather than ValueError; the rest of the list stayed as before.

lessons.text: Not every project in this repo has a `tests/` directory: a project may be a single tiny package (e.g. `greet/` with `hello.py`), in which case the CI `tests` check passes with no tests and lessons #1 (`test_regression_*`) and #4 (`tests/__init__.py`) only apply once tests exist or a bug is fixed.
lessons.evidence: This session's project was a `greet/` package with `__init__.py` + `hello.py` and no `tests/` at all; my one-line change passed the CI `tests` check with no tests present, so `test_regression_*` (lesson #1) and `tests/__init__.py` (lesson #4) did not apply here.

lessons.text: The `tests` CI check runs as `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, so module-level env validation never fails in CI; run the suite locally with the variable unset as well, since that is where import-time env checks break.
lessons.evidence: This session's CI report was "✓ tests (APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .)". Running that same command locally passed only after my fix, while the plain run without APP_ENV first failed with `RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None` from billing/settings.py — CI would never have shown that failure.

lessons.text: When the suite fails with an import/collection error rather than an assertion, learn the whole failure chain before editing: re-run with a value that satisfies the import-time guard (e.g. `APP_ENV=test python -m unittest ...`) or import the module directly, note every hidden failure, fix them, then re-run the plain command.
lessons.evidence: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` failed with `RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None` (import error) and hid the real bug; re-running as `APP_ENV=test python -m unittest ...` revealed `AssertionError: 3.0 != 2.0` from the stray `+ 1` in billing/tax.py, so I fixed both bugs in one pass instead of iterating blind.

lessons.text: This repo's CI has a `mypy/pydocstyle` check that fails on any new or changed function lacking full type annotations and/or a docstring ("missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring"); it does not flag untouched pre-existing functions. `mypy`/`pydocstyle` are not installed here (`No module named mypy`), so write annotated, docstringed definitions from the start and verify by importing the module.
lessons.evidence: CI report on my change: "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" — the function I added was unannotated in the style of the existing `shout`, which was never flagged. Adding `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str:` plus a docstring addresses it; `python3 -m mypy` and `python3 -m pydocstyle` both returned "No module named ..." so the gate cannot be re-run locally.

lessons.text: This repo's CI has an `error-policy` check that appears next to `tests` in the report; a change that raises the package's own error class from its `errors.py` (this session: `from users.errors import AppError`) passed it. When a task says "raise an exception", grep the package for an existing error class first and raise that instead of a builtin like `ValueError`.
lessons.evidence: Read of users/errors.py showed an unused `AppError(Exception)`; I raised AppError from validate_age instead of ValueError and the CI report came back "✓ tests / ✓ error-policy", confirming that choice satisfies the gate.

lessons.text: Before ending a turn with a change, self-check the known CI gates of this repo, since no CI config exists in the tree: (1) every added .py file starts with `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`; (2) no `print`/`warnings.warn` in library code (L001: use a module logger); (3) a bug-fix PR includes a test named `test_regression_*`; (4) if you created tests/, it has `tests/__init__.py`; (5) the final report ends with a `Risk: low|medium|high` line.
lessons.evidence: This session the only CI failure (release-bot: missing `Risk:` line) was one I could have caught before reporting, just as the earlier gate failures (#1 regression test naming, #2 license header, #3 L001) each surfaced only after I had already reported. I never ran such a self-check; adding one is backed by four separate failed reports.

lessons.text: Not every project in this repo has a `tests/` directory: a project may be a single tiny package (e.g. `greet/` with `hello.py`), in which case the CI `tests` check passes with no tests and lessons #1 (`test_regression_*`) and #4 (`tests/__init__.py`) only apply once tests exist or a bug is fixed.
lessons.evidence: This session's project was a `greet/` package with `__init__.py` + `hello.py` and no `tests/` at all; my one-line change passed the CI `tests` check with no tests present, so `test_regression_*` (lesson #1) and `tests/__init__.py` (lesson #4) did not apply here.

lessons.text: The working directory's project changes between sessions: it may be a small pure-Python package such as `inventory/` or `shapes/` (with tests in `tests/`, run by `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v`). Always read the tree first and match the conventions of sibling modules; do not trust a remembered package name, and do not assume a `CHANGELOG.md` exists.
lessons.evidence: Lesson #0 asserted the project was the `inventory` package, but this session's tree was `shapes/square.py` + empty `shapes/__init__.py` with no `tests/`; I had to `ls` and read `shapes/square.py` to learn the style, so the concrete package name in the lesson was misleading.

lessons.text: When creating the first `tests/` file in this repo, also add `tests/__init__.py` (with the `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` header); otherwise `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` fails with `ImportError: Start directory is not importable`.
lessons.evidence: In this session `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` first failed with `ImportError: Start directory is not importable: '.../tests'` because the repo had no `tests/` package; adding `tests/__init__.py` (header included per lesson #2) made discovery run the 2 tests.

lessons.text: End every final report of a turn with a line `Risk: low|medium|high`, on its own line, as the very last line (e.g. `Risk: low`), because the `release-bot` CI check fails the change when the final report has no such line.
lessons.evidence: CI report after the greet() change: "✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end", while the tests check passed.

lessons.text: Before ending a turn with a change, self-check the known CI gates of this repo, since no CI config exists in the tree: (1) every added .py file starts with `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`; (2) no `print`/`warnings.warn` in library code (L001: use a module logger); (3) a bug-fix PR includes a test named `test_regression_*`; (4) if you created tests/, it has `tests/__init__.py`; (5) every new or changed function has full type annotations and a docstring (mypy/pydocstyle gate, even if sibling functions lack them); (6) the final report ends with a `Risk: low|medium|high` line.
lessons.evidence: This session's only CI failure was the `mypy/pydocstyle` gate, which the old 5-item list did not cover: I added `reverse_words(s)` unannotated because the sibling `shout(s)` is unannotated, and CI rejected it. Adding the annotation/docstring gate to the checklist is backed by that failed report, just as (1)-(4) were backed by earlier ones.

lessons.text: Not every project in this repo has a `tests/` directory: a project may be a single tiny package (e.g. `greet/` with `hello.py`), in which case the CI `tests` check passes with no tests and lessons #1 (`test_regression_*`) and #4 (`tests/__init__.py`) only apply once tests exist or a bug is fixed.
lessons.evidence: This session's project was a `greet/` package with `__init__.py` + `hello.py` and no `tests/` at all; my one-line change passed the CI `tests` check with no tests present, so `test_regression_*` (lesson #1) and `tests/__init__.py` (lesson #4) did not apply here.

lessons.text: The `tests` CI check runs as `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, so module-level env validation never fails in CI; run the suite locally with the variable unset as well, since that is where import-time env checks break.
lessons.evidence: This session's CI report was "✓ tests (APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .)". Running that same command locally passed only after my fix, while the plain run without APP_ENV first failed with `RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None` from billing/settings.py — CI would never have shown that failure.

lessons.text: When the suite fails with an import/collection error rather than an assertion, learn the whole failure chain before editing: re-run with a value that satisfies the import-time guard (e.g. `APP_ENV=test python -m unittest ...`) or import the module directly, note every hidden failure, fix them, then re-run the plain command.
lessons.evidence: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` failed with `RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None` (import error) and hid the real bug; re-running as `APP_ENV=test python -m unittest ...` revealed `AssertionError: 3.0 != 2.0` from the stray `+ 1` in billing/tax.py, so I fixed both bugs in one pass instead of iterating blind.

lessons.text: This repo's CI has a `mypy/pydocstyle` check that fails on any new or changed function lacking full type annotations and/or a docstring ("missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring"); it does not flag untouched pre-existing functions. `mypy`/`pydocstyle` are not installed here (`No module named mypy`), so write annotated, docstringed definitions from the start and verify by importing the module.
lessons.evidence: CI report on my change: "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" — the function I added was unannotated in the style of the existing `shout`, which was never flagged. Adding `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str:` plus a docstring addresses it; `python3 -m mypy` and `python3 -m pydocstyle` both returned "No module named ..." so the gate cannot be re-run locally.

lessons.text: This repo's CI has an `error-policy` check that appears next to `tests` in the report; a change that raises the package's own error class from its `errors.py` (this session: `from users.errors import AppError`) passed it. When a task says "raise an exception", grep the package for an existing error class first and raise that instead of a builtin like `ValueError`.
lessons.evidence: Read of users/errors.py showed an unused `AppError(Exception)`; I raised AppError from validate_age instead of ValueError and the CI report came back "✓ tests / ✓ error-policy", confirming that choice satisfies the gate.
